messages:
Sam: Quick sync — I sketched a deterministic sort we can apply at gateway selection so route pick is stable across instances. Thoughts?
Zara: Nice, do you mean instead of random tie-break or creation-time? :thinking_face:
Sam: Exactly. Random breaks cache locality. Proposal: compute a sort key tuple per route and pick the highest lexicographically. Key components: (match_specificity, exact_segment_count, header_match_count, host_wildcard_score, negative_matches_penalty, route_id_hash)
Ben: Can you show a small example of how specificity is computed?
Sam: Sure — rough rules:
```
match_specificity = sum(segment_score for each path segment)
segment_score: exact=100, param=30, wildcard=10, regex=50
example: /users/:id/profile -> 100 + 30 + 100 = 230
```
Then tie-breakers: more exact segments wins; more header constraints wins; fewer negative matches wins. Finally stable hash of route id as last tiebreaker.
Nina: I like making it deterministic. Two questions: 1) how do we rank host globs vs explicit host? 2) what about performance for large rule sets?
Sam: For host: explicit host gets high host_score (200), single-star gets 50, multi-glob gets 20. For performance: precompute the sort_key at config load and store as 64-bit tuple; selection is then a single compare op.
Zara: What about regex routes that are more expressive but should they outrank a simple prefix? Regex had higher score above, but that seems subjective.
Ben: Could we add a configurable policy per domain/team? e.g., default policy is prefix-first, infra can opt in to regex-priority.
Sam: Yeah, propose we add a per-space override: `route_policy: deterministic_sort_v1 | legacy_first_match | regex_priority`. Default deterministic_sort_v1 described here.
Nina: Edge case: overlapping routes with different methods (GET vs POST). We already match method first right?
Sam: Yes method + content-type remain pre-filters. Sort only applies to routes that are otherwise compatible (same method + header scope).
Zara: Implementation note: maintain stable ordering when we hot-reload a route — we must compute route_id_hash from a stable UUID assigned at create-time, not from file path.
deploy-bot: CI check triggered: lint/gateway-sorts passed on PR #4821 :white_check_mark:
Ben: UX: can we expose a `why-chosen` trace in Console? e.g., show the sort key and competing routes. That would help debug.
Sam: Agreed — Console panel: matched routes + their keys, and arrow to the winner. I can prototype.
Nina: One more: fallback policy when no route matches — current behavior is 404, but some teams want service-default fallback. We should ensure deterministic sort does not interfere with fallback routing.
Sam: Good call. Fallbacks remain a separate bucket that is considered after deterministic selection.
Zara: LGTM overall. If we land this, add a migration that computes keys and an integration test with randomized rule orders to assert stability.
Ben: I'll add tests simulating 10k-routes and assert pick consistency across shuffles.
Sam: Thanks — I'll open a draft RFC with examples and the sort key algebra.
Nina: Thanks Sam.
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/472-deterministic-gateway-sorting
